output.brief: The rejections were most likely caused by a data error in our own booking system. On 1 Aug the contractor created the Tallis mandarin product record by copying the avocado record, and the 7.0°C carriage temperature was left in. You can see this in the change history. Our specification for mandarins is 4.0°C. Every Meridane container booked through Tallis went out at 7.0°C, and the carrier's controllers held that setpoint. All five of those containers were rejected, with decay of 9–14%. The four containers booked by email at 4.0°C all passed, on both carriers and with both old and new fungicide. So the new fungicide, Meridane's equipment, the transit time and the Lower Serra storm fruit don't explain the pattern. The Lower Serra pallets did show more decay inside the rejected containers. That may be a secondary effect, but it is not a reason to suspend them. I am quite sure of this conclusion, though not certain. Next steps: fix the Tallis mandarin record to 4.0°C now. Have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check of reefer settings against the product specification before each booking is submitted. Hold off on the cargo claim, the Lower Serra suspension and the fungicide reversal. Tell Nordhafen what happened and what has been fixed.
